transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-30
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Rivermark Head of ML), Priya Nair (Infra), Liam Murphy (SRE)

Summary:
Quick sync on POC latency tuning progress — focused on TTFT (time-to-first-token), streaming mode behavior, sequence length effects, and kernel selection/quantization impacts. Agreed next experiments and owners.

Topics:
- TTFT regressions seen on 2k->4k sequences
- Streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs for user-facing API
- Kernel selection: bf16 vs int8 quant kernels and attention kernel choice (fused v. block)
- Batching behavior and autoscale/clustering interactions

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this tight 45 min, quick recap from last week and then dig into the TTFT numbers Maya pulled.
[00:12] Sam: sounds good, we have a hard SLO for first token under 200ms, p95 under 350ms, so that's the bar.
[00:20] Maya: yep, I ran the 2k and 4k job sets overnight, uploaded the sheet — link in the chat — bench sheet has raw traces, i left notes about the run config.
[00:32] Priya: got it, we looked at the high level, looks like p50 is fine but p95 popped on 4k in streaming.
[00:40] Maya: yeah so the main thing is TTFT increased because the model warms the KV cache and attention kernel chosen on our infra path for long sequences fell back to a less optimal kernel. there's also some extra memcpy between devices in the config we tested.
[00:57] Liam: memcpy? you mean between GPU and host or between GPUs?
[01:00] Maya: between GPU shards for the sharded kv path — so more cross-device transfers for 4k with our current sharding layout, that added like 30-60ms depending on batch.
[01:12] Sam: hmm, okay. can we change sharding or is that fixed by the Dedicated setup?
[01:18] Maya: you can change the sharding policy, and on Dedicated we can pin a policy that avoids cross-GPU transfers for the first chunk. but tradeoff is throughput efficiency.
[01:27] Jordan: quick note, this is exactly why the Dedicated pool can help — predictable topology reduces the fallback kernel incidence.
[01:33] Priya: we're sensitive to cost though, show us the tradeoffs please.
[01:37] Jordan: will do, i'll send a small matrix after the call.

[05:12] Maya: ok back to numbers — for 2k sequence, ttft median ~78ms, p95 ~160ms; for 4k in streaming mode median ~120ms, p95 ~420ms. non-streaming generation has higher median but lower p95 in some runs because batching absorbed variance.
[05:32] Sam: interesting, so streaming actually worsened p95 at 4k?
[05:36] Maya: right, streaming reduces token latency for the emitted tail, but the initial token path triggers extra kernel selection and we saw fallback to a slower attention kernel on our runtime for that path. the runtime isn't perfectly picking the fused attention variant for 4k in that config.
[05:51] Liam: is that a runtime bug or expected behavior?
[05:55] Maya: probably matchup of heuristics + memory footprint. when sequences cross certain thresholds our kernel selector chooses a block-attn kernel that has higher start latency but better amortized throughput. we need a heuristic tweak for TTFT-priority workloads.

[08:20] Sam: ok, what about quantization? we tried int8 4-bit earlier — did that change TTFT?
[08:27] Maya: quant helps throughput and cost but int8 quant introduces dequant/decompress steps that can bump TTFT. in our tests int8 reduced overall token cost by ~40% but added 20-40ms to TTFT for first token in some paths. bf16 had near-native TTFT but higher cost.
[08:45] Priya: so hybrid approach? maybe bf16 for latency-critical endpoints and int8 for background tasks?
[08:50] Jordan: that's a common pattern — classify routes. Redwood supports per-route model variants so you can route latency-critical calls to bf16 variants and cheap bulk to int8.

[12:12] Maya: another lever is KV prefix caching — if you can cache the prefix KV for common prompts, TTFT for subsequent calls drops dramatically. We saw ~60-70ms saving when cache hit. but cache invalidation and privacy constraints are something to discuss.
[12:30] Sam: we could do prefix caching only for system prompts and not user PII content, that might be workable.

[15:05] Priya: curious about batching, we run bursts — does batching hurt TTFT?
[15:10] Maya: batching increases throughput efficiency but can increase single-request latency as it waits to fill batch windows. Redwood has a low-latency continuous batching mode; for strict TTFT you can set batching off or small batch windows. For our tests we compared batching off vs 5ms vs 20ms batch window.
[15:28] Sam: results?
[15:30] Maya: off: p50/p95 80/160; 5ms window: 75/150; 20ms window: 65/340 — so large windows create tail regressions.

[19:00] Liam: what about autoscale warm pools? our production sees cold scale ups which we don't want.
[19:06] Jordan: Dedicated can reserve warm capacity and provide burst, also cold start mitigation via pre-warmed replicas. There's a cost hit but it's predictable.
[19:18] Priya: ok, we need numbers for cost vs latency for that config.
[19:21] Jordan: noted, i'll add to the matrix.

[23:40] Maya: action item for kernel profiling — we want to capture profiler traces when a 4k request comes in, see where the time is spent (copy, kernel, scheduling). if it's the kernel choice we can modify the selector heuristics or force a fused kernel for that path.
[23:55] Sam: can we force it for a subset of requests?
[23:58] Maya: yep, we can pin model variant with a forced kernel/quantization profile at route level for the POC.

[28:10] Priya: one more question: streaming vs chunked — any impact on client SDKs?
[28:15] Jordan: SDK supports both; streaming reduces client-side latency but you have to manage partial outputs. we have examples in the quickstart for node/java/python streaming handlers.

[33:00] Sam: okay fallback scenario — if Dedicated isn't approved, can we still meet SLOs on Hosted?
[33:08] Maya: possible but harder. Hosted has multi-tenant variability and more conservative kernel fallbacks. We saw a 10-20% higher p95 in Hosted runs versus Dedicated-simulated topology for the same model. For strict SLOs you probably need Dedicated or at least a reserved warm pool.
[33:25] Sam: noted. competitor question — have you benchmarked against Anthropic / Bedrock?
[33:30] Jordan: yes we've got some public benchmarks; i'll include a short slide but we focused on our kernel and runtime differences — results vary by model and prompt.

[36:40] Maya: to be concrete, next experiments I propose: 1) TTFT run with sequence=4096, shared KV and enforced fused attention kernel, no batching; 2) Streaming run with small batch window (5ms) and bf16; 3) Int8 run to profile dequant cost on TTFT. i'll post the configs and scripts.
[36:58] Priya: good. also we'll share a sample trace so you can reproduce the exact request distribution.

[40:05] Jordan: ok, let's recap next steps — Maya runs those three experiments and posts results, Jordan sends Dedicated cost/latency matrix, Rivermark shares traces. We'll schedule the kernel profiling session next week.
[40:20] Sam: thanks folks, that works for us.
[40:23] Maya: one last bit — i left a note in the bench sheet about a slight transcription of the run id, the file name is run_20271130_rapid.json in the sheet.
[40:33] Liam: got it. thanks.
[40:36] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with the links and next meeting invite.

End of transcript.
